newsitem.title: INDONESIA: India calls for exploration bids for crude, gas.
newsitem.headline: India calls for exploration bids for crude, gas.

text.p: India will offer 31 offshore blocks and 25 coal-bed methane blocks for exploration and production, Indian officials said on Wednesday.
The officials, part of a visiting delegation from India's Petroleum and Natural Gas ministry, told reporters that the offshore blocks will be offered in the third week of August.

All blocks will be on offer under the government's New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP), which provides large incentives for investing in India's energy sector, said T.R. Baalu, minister of state for petroleum and natural gas.
The offshore blocks on offer are in the Andaman and Nicobar, Bengal, Mumbai, Cauvery, Kerala-Konkan, Gujarat-Kutch, Krishna-Godavari, Mahanadi, Palar and Saurashtra basins, the officials said.

The coal-bed methane (CBM) blocks are at Raniganj, Jharia, East and West Bokaro, Satpura, Sohagpur, Talcher, Wardha Valley, Godavari Valley and Neyveli and in tertiary coalfields of northeastern India and Jammu, they said.
Petroleum Minister Janeshwar Mishra said in New Delhi on Tuesday that the bids for the CBM projects will be invited by the end of the year.

CBM is a hydrocarbon gas recovered from coal seams and is identical to natural gas, which contains up to 95 percent methane. However, unlike natural gas, it does not exist as compressed gas and is recovered through dewatering coal.

Baalu said the incentives under the NELP included a five-year tax holiday extendable to seven years in northeastern India, the abolition of local tax, open availability of exploration acreages, royalties fixed at ad valorem prices and no mandatory participation of Indian state-owned companies.
Royalty has been fixed at 10 percent for offshore areas and 12.5 percent onshore, he said. Royalty payment for natural gas for both offshore and onshore areas will be ten percent, Baalu added.
To encourage exploration in deep-water and frontier areas, royalty will be charged at half the prevailing rate for the first seven years after commencement of commercial production, he said.
The government has also said it is preparing a model production-sharing contract and a petroleum tax code.
"It is one of the best policies offered anywhere in the world," Baalu said.
